name: Rapeman
label: Touch and Go
lede: Rapeman lasted two years and put out one EP and one album, and the name got Steve Albini's trio picketed in 1988 and, by his own 2020 account, indefensible.

eras.title: Big Black ends, Scratch Acid moves north
eras.text: Big Black broke up in 1987 and Scratch Acid fell apart in Austin the same year. Its bassist and drummer moved to Chicago, and Steve Albini had a new trio within months.

years.h: Albini and two Scratch Acid veterans start a trio in Chicago
years.p: After Big Black's split, Steve Albini teams with bassist [[David Wm. Sims|c6c8a98f-9cfb-4fad-a657-880245ff15d3]] and drummer [[Rey Washam|33b09380-db28-4c9c-9fdd-ab5c20049c61]], both just out of Austin's Scratch Acid and newly moved to Chicago.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rapeman · Wikipedia: David Wm. Sims
years.h: Albini names the band after a manga he found repellent
years.p: Albini and Washam were fixated on a Japanese comic, The Rapeman, that Albini came across through an import-business contact. The name was meant to repel audiences and needle bands chasing MTV.
years.xp:
Albini has said he found the manga "simultaneously utterly repellent and fascinating", and described it as the product of decades of repression and misogyny expressed through a different cultural tradition.

He later called the name a flippant choice. In a 2020 podcast interview he went further, calling it unconscionable and indefensible, and said he felt he'd never been held to account for it. Sims, in a 2014 podcast, said he'd always had issues with the name.

eras.title: One year, one cat in the credits
eras.text: Rapeman put out everything it would release in 1988: an EP, half of it live, and an album whose sleeve credits Albini's cat as producer. Albini was also becoming the engineer every band wanted, and the name followed the trio to every town.

years.h: Rapeman's first record is built on R. Budd Dwyer's press conference
years.p: Budd takes its seven-minute title track from R. Budd Dwyer, the Pennsylvania state treasurer who shot himself at a televised press conference in 1987. Three of the four songs were recorded live.
years.xp: Pitchfork later ranked Budd sixth on its list of Steve Albini's ten best records, crediting its empty spaces and grainy textures with setting a template for 1990s post-rock.

years.src: Wikipedia: Two Nuns and a Pack Mule
yt: Rapeman live on WZRD-FM Chicago, July 1988
years.h: The producer credit on Two Nuns and a Pack Mule goes to a cat
years.p: Ten songs on Touch and Go (Blast First in the UK), including a cover of [[ZZ Top|a81259a0-a2f5-464b-866e-71220f2739f1]]'s Just Got Paid. The sleeve credits Albini and Fluss; Fluss turned out to be Albini's cat.
years.xp: Kerry Crafton engineered. The vinyl sleeve swapped Marmoset and Radar Love Lizard in the track listing, and the CD tacked on the whole Budd EP. FACT later ranked it the 28th best album of the 1980s.
play: Two Nuns and a Pack Mule

years.cap: Steve Albini with Rapeman at City Gardens, Trenton, New Jersey, 1988
years.p: The New Jersey club show on September 24, 1988 survives on tape and is now part of the McKenzie Tapes archive.
years.xp: The Maxwell's tape was restored and mastered for release, and the full set is up on YouTube.

years.h: John Peel sees Rapeman at the Mean Fiddler and writes it up
years.p: Peel reviewed the north London show for The Observer: a miserable choice of name, he said, and a set so intense that plain applause felt faintly insulting.
years.xp:
The name dogged the tour. The Chicago Punk Database says many American shows were met by picket lines of women, and a sold-out show in England nearly got cancelled over a student boycott. By some accounts the controversy only pulled bigger crowds.

A show at Oliver's in Chester on October 12, 1988 was later released as a live record.

eras.title: Three exits
eras.text: Rapeman ended in 1989 over personal friction, not the name, according to accounts of the band. Its three members went on to shape the next decade of noise rock from Chicago.

years.h: The last release is a Sub Pop Singles Club 7", Inki's Butt Crack
years.p: Rapeman's last release goes out as a Sub Pop Singles Club subscription single.

years.h: Rapeman ends, and Sims goes back to Yow
years.p: Sims teams back up with his Scratch Acid singer [[David Yow|81af2517-4481-4960-a337-213e1f8b5a61]] in [[The Jesus Lizard|dfebd6c0-dae7-4cc8-a8e9-0dbaa382209f]]. [[Rey Washam|33b09380-db28-4c9c-9fdd-ab5c20049c61]] goes on to the [[Didjits|e3d01dcb-eb41-4ce9-8506-bfd70aa8d651]], [[Ministry|13df2a46-f72f-40e7-aa63-26fcf62c7048]] and [[Helios Creed|26a13357-fad6-4900-a324-ff252e681112]].

eras.title: The engineer and the apology
eras.text: Albini built Shellac and a recording career that ran from the Pixies to Nirvana. Rapeman became the part of his story he stopped defending.

years.h: Sims puts the name down as his biggest musical regret
years.p: In a 2014 podcast, the former Rapeman and Jesus Lizard bassist, by then a New York accountant, says he always had problems with the band's name.

yt: Albini on the band name and being held to account for it
years.h: Albini compares the name to a bad tattoo
years.p: On a 2020 podcast, Albini calls it a flippant choice he can't defend, and says he was never held to account for it.
years.xp: He called the name unconscionable and indefensible. By 2021, per Wikipedia, he was saying he'd been ignorant of women's issues and had wrongly assumed such problems were already solved.

years.p: Albini died at 61, days before [[Shellac|604f273a-d3c1-4b5b-ab83-99541f9368ea]] released To All Trains. His Electrical Audio studio said the cause was a heart attack.
